lateral_torso_line_topology.vertical_line_count_and_spacing: Approximately 4 distinct white vertical lines are visible on the lateral torso. Spacing is wider between the anterior-most line and the second line, with closer, more irregular spacing between the posterior lines.
lateral_torso_line_topology.discontinuity_mapping: The anterior-most line appears as a series of three short dashed segments. Central lines are discontinuous where they meet the ventral fringe hair and are partially occluded by avian presence.

posterior_constellation_clusters.spatial_cluster_density: A cluster of approximately 6-8 high-contrast white spots is visible on the posterior haunch and upper hind limb, concentrated above the white inguinal patch.
posterior_constellation_clusters.linear_blob_alignment: Three distinct spots on the mid-thigh align to form a short, semi-connected diagonal geometric line sloping towards the posterior.

macro_horn_vector_geometry.curve_trajectory_2d: The visible horn follows an upward and posterior trajectory with a lyrate curve, oriented at approximately 55 degrees relative to the skull base.
macro_horn_vector_geometry.terminal_contrast_ratio: The high-contrast ivory tip constitutes approximately 12-15% of the total visible length of the horn structure.

other_distinctive_markers: Two oxpecker birds are attached to the mid-lateral torso. Contrast-heavy white markings are visible on the muzzle and between the eyes. Limbs exhibit a sharp transition to orange-tan coloration below the carpal and tarsal joints.
